library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Motoki_2019_dotinurad"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Motoki_2019_dotinurad"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.533> (open access)

Dotinurad is a selective URAT1 inhibitor that lowers serum urate (SUA) by
blocking renal tubular reabsorption of urate. Motoki 2019 fitted a
one-compartment oral PK model to fasted single-dose data and coupled it to a
physiological urate mass balance (Figure 1 of the paper): urate is produced at
a constant rate, leaves by a constant non-renal (gut) route and by the kidney,
and dotinurad raises renal urate clearance by inhibiting reabsorption of the
filtered load with a simple Emax function of plasma concentration (Eq. 8):

$$CL_{R,UA} = GFR - f_{reabs} \cdot GFR \cdot \left(1 - \frac{E_{max} C_p}{EC_{50} + C_p}\right)$$

The model was built on the single ascending dose (SAD) study and validated by
predicting SUA in the multiple ascending dose (MAD) study.

# Population

Both studies enrolled healthy Japanese men aged 20-35 years with a body mass
index of 18.5 to < 25.0 kg/m^2. The SAD study (NCT02348307) randomised 54
subjects to single fasted oral doses of 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 or 20 mg (6 per dose)
or placebo (3 per dose level), with a fed 5 mg period in the same subjects. The
MAD study (NCT02348333) gave 2 or 5 mg (6 per dose) or placebo (3 per dose)
once daily for 7 days under fed conditions. Mean (SD) pre-dose values across
the SAD study were SUA 5.71 (0.75) mg/dL, 24-h urinary urate excretion (XuUA)
575 (100) mg/day and renal urate clearance (CLRUA) 7.10 (1.51) mL/min
(Motoki 2019 Results). Mean body weight in the SAD study was about 60 kg
(Discussion). The paper prints no table of baseline demographics.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Motoki_2019_dotinurad")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Motoki_2019_dotinurad.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | log(0.770) 1/h | Table 3, Ka |
| `lvc` | log(10.585) L | Table 3, V/F = 10 585 mL |
| `lkel` | log(0.0795) 1/h | Table 3, Ke |
| `lvd_urate` | log(16.0) L | Table 3, VdUA (Eq. 4) |
| `f_reab_urate` | 0.943 | Table 3, freabs (Eq. 9) |
| `lemax` | log(0.51) | Table 3, Emax |
| `lec50` | log(196) ng/mL | Table 3, EC50 |
| `lksyn` | log(35.9375) mg/h, fixed | Eq. 7: Synthesis = 3/2 x XuUA, with XuUA = 575 mg/day (Results) |
| `lcl_nonren_urate` | log(0.213) L/h, fixed | Eq. 6: CLGutUA = 1/2 x CLRUA, with CLRUA = 7.10 mL/min (Results) |
| `lrbase` | log(5.71) mg/dL, fixed | Results, mean baseline SUA; initial value of the urate pool (Model simulation section) |
| `CRCL` (covariate) | GFR | Methods: Ccr adjusted to 1.73 m^2 used as GFR |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Methods: one-compartment model with first-order absorption |
| `cl_renal_urate` | n/a | Eq. 8 |
| `d/dt(urate)` | n/a | Eq. 1-3 (Figure 1), in differential form |
| `urate(0)` | n/a | Model simulation: observed mean baseline SUA as initial value; initial UApool from Eq. 1 |

# Typical subject

The paper does not print the cohort's creatinine clearance. Equation 9 gives
the pre-dose renal urate clearance as `GFR * (1 - freabs)`, so the printed mean
baseline CLRUA of 7.10 mL/min and freabs of 0.943 imply the GFR used below.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Motoki_2019_dotinurad")
crcl_typ <- 7.10 / (1 - 0.943)
crcl_typ

# Deterministic identity: the model's pre-dose renal clearance reproduces
# the printed 7.10 mL/min exactly.
stopifnot(abs(crcl_typ * (1 - 0.943) - 7.10) < 1e-10)
```

The model is a typical-value model (no random effects and no residual error), so
every simulation below is deterministic.

# Single ascending dose study

```{r sad-sim}
sad_doses <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), seq(12, 96, by = 0.5))))

make_sad <- function(dose, id) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = dose, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      CRCL = crcl_typ,
      treatment = paste(dose, "mg")
    )
}
sad_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(sad_doses), function(i) make_sad(sad_doses[i], i)),
  # placebo: zero dose, so the urate pool is left to its own dynamics
  make_sad(0, length(sad_doses) + 1L) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Placebo")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
sad_levels <- c("Placebo", paste(sad_doses, "mg"))

sad <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = sad_events, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = sad_levels))
```

## Figure 2: dotinurad plasma concentrations

```{r figure-2}
sad |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "Placebo", time <= 48, time >= 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1e4)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Dotinurad plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Dose",
    caption = "Replicates the model-predicted lines of Figure 2 of Motoki 2019."
  )
```

## NCA against Table 1

```{r sad-nca}
sad_nca <- sad |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "Placebo", !is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment))
sad_dose <- sad_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, treatment != "Placebo") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

sad_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sad_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(sad_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
))

table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~half.life, ~aucinf.obs,
  "0.5 mg", 41.5, 2.67, 9.67, 613,
  "1 mg", 89.2, 3.33, 9.60, 1276,
  "2 mg", 175.2, 3.10, 9.53, 2599,
  "5 mg", 447.8, 2.00, 9.27, 5526,
  "10 mg", 858.2, 3.25, 9.87, 12126,
  "20 mg", 1783.6, 2.25, 10.65, 23398
)

sad_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sad_res,
  reference = table1,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", half.life = "h", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  sad_cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Typical-value simulation vs. Motoki 2019 Table 1 (observed mean, fasted).",
    "* differs from reference by > 20%."
  )
)
```

AUC0-inf is reproduced within about 10% at every dose, which is what the
printed V/F and Ke jointly determine (CL/F = Ke x V/F = 0.842 L/h against a
mean observed CL/F of 0.850 L/h). Cmax runs 12-19% below the observed means at
every dose and t1/2 (8.7 h, i.e. ln 2 / Ke) runs below the observed 9.3-10.7 h;
both are properties of the one-compartment fit, and the paper's own predicted
lines in Figure 2 show the same shortfall at the peak. Tmax is a sampled value
in the observed data and is not compared closely.

```{r sad-nca-check}
auc_cmp <- sad_res$result |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table1, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (PPORRES / aucinf.obs - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(auc_cmp) == 6L)
# Deterministic: measured -9% to +8%. A mis-transcribed V/F or Ke moves
# every dose by the same tens of percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_cmp$pct) < 15))
```

## Figure 3 and the uricosuric response

```{r figure-3}
sad |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 48) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, sUA, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 12)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 7)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "SUA (mg/dL)", colour = "Dose",
    caption = paste(
      "Model counterpart of Figure 3 of Motoki 2019 (the figure shows observed",
      "means only), typical subject starting from the SAD mean baseline 5.71 mg/dL."
    )
  )
```

The paper reports the following ranges across the six dose groups (Results):
the maximal decrease in SUA within 48 h was 1.6-4.2 mg/dL, XuUA over 0-24 h
was 869-1458 mg, and CLRUA over 0-24 h was 12.1-47.9 mL/min, with all three
effects close to maximal at 5 mg. CLRUA over an interval is computed as in the
paper's PD analysis, XuUA / AUEC.

```{r sad-pd}
auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
sad_pd <- sad |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "Placebo") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_decrease = 5.71 - min(sUA[time <= 48]),
    xu_0_24 = urate_urine[time == 24] - urate_urine[time == 0],
    # mg / (mg/dL * h) = dL/h; x 100 / 60 gives mL/min
    clr_0_24 = xu_0_24 / auc_trap(time[time <= 24], sUA[time <= 24]) * 100 / 60,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(
  sad_pd |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose" = treatment,
      "Maximal SUA decrease, 0-48 h (mg/dL)" = max_decrease,
      "XuUA 0-24 h (mg)" = xu_0_24,
      "CLRUA 0-24 h (mL/min)" = clr_0_24
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Typical-value SAD urate response by dose."
)

# Deterministic. The paper's reported ranges run from the lowest to the
# highest dose group; the model's 0.5 mg and 20 mg values sit at
# -9%/+9% (SUA decrease), -2%/+2% (XuUA) and +6%/+14% (CLRUA) of them.
lo <- sad_pd[sad_pd$treatment == "0.5 mg", ]
hi <- sad_pd[sad_pd$treatment == "20 mg", ]
stopifnot(
  nrow(lo) == 1L, nrow(hi) == 1L,
  abs(lo$xu_0_24 / 869 - 1) < 0.10, abs(hi$xu_0_24 / 1458 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(lo$max_decrease / 1.6 - 1) < 0.20, abs(hi$max_decrease / 4.2 - 1) < 0.20,
  abs(lo$clr_0_24 / 12.1 - 1) < 0.25, abs(hi$clr_0_24 / 47.9 - 1) < 0.25
)
```

The placebo arm shows the consequence of treating urate production and
non-renal clearance as constants derived from cohort means: the typical
subject's urate steady state is `ksyn / (CLRUA + CLGutUA)` = 5.62 mg/dL, not
exactly the mean baseline of 5.71 mg/dL, because a ratio of means (575 mg/day
over 7.10 mL/min) is not the mean of the ratios.

```{r placebo}
pbo <- sad |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "Placebo")
ss_typ <- 35.9375 / (crcl_typ * 0.06 * (1 - 0.943) + 0.213) / 10
ss_typ
stopifnot(abs(pbo$sUA[pbo$time == 96] / 5.71 - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Multiple ascending dose study

## PK against Table 2

```{r mad-sim}
mad_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 0.1), seq(168, 216, by = 1))))
make_mad <- function(dose, id, sua0) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = 24 * (0:6), evid = 1, amt = dose, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = id, time = mad_times, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      CRCL = crcl_typ,
      treatment = paste(dose, "mg")
    )
}
# Each arm starts from its own observed baseline SUA (read off Figure 4:
# 6.45 mg/dL at 2 mg, 6.85 mg/dL at 5 mg), as the paper's simulation did.
mad_2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = make_mad(2, 1L), keep = "treatment",
                         params = c(lrbase = log(6.45)))
mad_5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = make_mad(5, 2L), keep = "treatment",
                         params = c(lrbase = log(6.85)))
# A single-subject solve returns no id column, so add it back
mad <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(mad_2) |> dplyr::mutate(id = 1L),
  as.data.frame(mad_5) |> dplyr::mutate(id = 2L)
)
mad_dose <- dplyr::bind_rows(make_mad(2, 1L), make_mad(5, 2L)) |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

mad_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    mad |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment),
    Cc ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(mad_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = c(0, 72, 144), end = c(24, 96, 168),
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
  )
))

mad_sim <- mad_res$result |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = paste("Day", c(`0` = 1, `72` = 4, `144` = 7)[as.character(start)])) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, day, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~day, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast,
  "2 mg", "Day 1", 188, 3.50, 2195,
  "2 mg", "Day 4", 224, 3.67, 2649,
  "2 mg", "Day 7", 228, 3.67, 2680,
  "5 mg", "Day 1", 438, 4.17, 5211,
  "5 mg", "Day 4", 493, 4.00, 6164,
  "5 mg", "Day 7", 514, 3.83, 6321
)
mad_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = mad_sim,
  reference = table2,
  by = c("treatment", "day"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  mad_cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Typical-value simulation vs. Motoki 2019 Table 2 (observed mean, fed;",
    "AUClast over each 24-h dosing interval is the paper's AUC0-24).",
    "* differs from reference by > 20%."
  )
)
```

The fasted single-dose PK model reproduces the fed multiple-dose AUC0-24 within
12% on every day, consistent with the paper's statements that fed exposure
was predictable from the fasted parameters and that the MAD concentrations were
close to the predictions (supplementary Figure S1). Cmax runs 12-24% below the
observed means, the same one-compartment shortfall at the peak seen after single
doses; at 2 mg it crosses the 20% flag on every day. The observed accumulation
ratio of 1.18-1.22 compares with 1/(1 - exp(-24 Ke)) = 1.17 for the model.

```{r mad-nca-check}
mad_auc <- mad_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table2, by = c("treatment", "day")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (PPORRES / auclast - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(mad_auc) == 6L, all(abs(mad_auc$pct) < 15))
```

## Figure 4: SUA after multiple doses

The paper's predicted SUA lines in Figure 4 were digitised by the maintainers
at time points away from the observed markers.

```{r figure-4}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~`2 mg`, ~`5 mg`,
  18, 2.89, 1.81,
  21, 2.89, 1.77,
  30, 2.35, 1.40,
  42, 2.19, 1.33,
  54, 2.09, 1.27,
  66, 2.12, 1.31,
  90, 2.10, 1.31,
  102, 2.05, 1.25,
  126, 2.06, 1.25,
  138, 2.12, 1.32,
  160, 2.03, 1.27,
  174, 2.72, 1.77,
  186, 3.51, 2.45,
  200, 4.35, 3.33,
  210, 4.87, 3.96
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "treatment", values_to = "paper")

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = mad, aes(time, sUA)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4, aes(time, paper), shape = 1, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 24)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 8)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "SUA (mg/dL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Motoki 2019. Line: packaged model.",
      "Open circles: the paper's predicted line, digitised."
    )
  )

fig4_cmp <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    mad |> dplyr::select(treatment, time, sUA),
    by = c("treatment", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sUA / paper - 1))
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median % diff` = median(pct),
    `Max abs % diff` = max(abs(pct)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Packaged model vs. the digitised Figure 4 prediction.")

# Deterministic. Measured median -5.8% (2 mg) and +7.2% (5 mg), max 9.6%.
# The alternative reading in which production is re-derived from each arm's
# own baseline gives +8% and +30%, so this gate separates the two readings.
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig4_cmp) == 30L,
  all(abs(tapply(fig4_cmp$pct, fig4_cmp$treatment, median)) < 10),
  max(abs(fig4_cmp$pct)) < 15
)
```

The packaged model follows the paper's prediction through the dosing week and
the 72-h washout, sitting about 6% below it at 2 mg and 7% above it at 5 mg.
The paper's simulation used each MAD arm's own mean baseline CLRUA, which is
not printed; the typical-subject GFR used here comes from the SAD study, and a
different arm-specific GFR shifts the two arms in the way seen.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Urate production and non-renal clearance are constants.** Equations 5-7
  derive Synthesis (3/2 x XuUA) and CLGutUA (1/2 x CLRUA) from pre-dose
  values, and the Model simulation section says SUA was predicted "using
  'Synthesis' in the scheme and VdUA as the constant value". The model uses
  the SAD study's printed mean pre-dose values (XuUA 575 mg/day, CLRUA
  7.10 mL/min), giving 862.5 mg/day (35.9375 mg/h) and 3.55 mL/min
  (0.213 L/h). The maintainers chose this over re-deriving production from each
  subject's own baseline for two reasons: it reproduces the paper's Figure 4
  prediction (median -6%/+7% against +8%/+30%), and only with constant
  production does a change in GFR change the urate steady state, which is the
  application to renal impairment that the paper's Discussion proposes. A
  user simulating a population whose pre-dose urate turnover differs from
  healthy Japanese men should override `lksyn` and `lcl_nonren_urate` with
  values derived by Eq. 6-7 from that population's baseline XuUA and CLRUA.
- **GFR.** CRCL is not printed. The typical value 124.6 mL/min/1.73 m^2 is
  back-calculated from Eq. 9 with the printed mean baseline CLRUA and freabs.
- **Initial urate pool.** The pool starts at the observed baseline SUA
  (`lrbase`, default 5.71 mg/dL), as in the paper. The MAD baselines (6.45 and
  6.85 mg/dL) were read off the first observed point in Figure 4.
- **Continuous-time mass balance.** The paper updated CLRUA every hour and
  stepped the cumulative urate amounts of Eq. 1 forward in discrete intervals;
  the packaged model integrates the same balance as an ODE driven by the
  instantaneous plasma concentration. The paper's Emax fit used the mean
  concentration over each urine collection interval.
- **Units.** Plasma dotinurad is returned in ng/mL (`Cc = 1000 * central /
  vc`, with V/F converted from 10 585 mL to 10.585 L) to match EC50. SUA is
  returned as `sUA` in mg/dL; `urate_urine` is the cumulative renal urate
  excretion in mg.
- **Food.** The PK parameters come from fasted data. The paper found fed
  exposure (5 mg; Cmax ratio 0.84, AUC ratio 0.95) well predicted by them and
  applied them unchanged to the fed MAD study; no food effect is encoded.
- **Variability.** The paper reports no between-subject or residual
  variability for the model; the %CV values in Table 3 are estimation
  uncertainty for the PK, Emax and EC50 parameters, and for VdUA (36.6%) and
  freabs (0.6%) the spread of the individual calculations from Eq. 4 and 9.
  None is encoded as a random effect.
- **Parameter naming.** `f_reab_urate` and `lvd_urate` follow the
  fraction-reabsorbed (`f_reab_water`) and analyte-volume (`vd_creatinine`)
  spellings of the Takita 2020 creatinine models.
- No erratum or correction notice for Motoki 2019 was found as of 2026-11-26.
